newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA TRACTOR SALES PICK UP IN JULY - SAAMA.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA TRACTOR SALES PICK UP IN JULY - SAAMA.

text.p: South African tractor sales recovered in July after three months of lower-than-expected figures, the South African Agricultural Machinery Association (SAAMA) said on Friday.
The month saw 548 units sold, a jump of 18 percent on July last year. Sales for the year so far stand at 3,266, a 0.7 percent drop on the 3,288 sales seen by this time in 1996.
SAAMA said the country's delayed harvest was proceding apace and yields are proving to be better than forecast.

The association said the tractor market was in a buying phase as summer crop prospects were boosting sentiment. "Good prospects for the forthcoming wheat crop should maintain buyer confidence in the market," SAAMA said.
However, baler and combine harvester sales are well down on last year. In the year so far 168 balers have been sold, down 36.4 percent on last year, and just 147 harvesters, down 25.8 percent.
"Baler sales continue to be disappointing, having been adversely affected by the poor haymaking and baling conditions whic have prevailed for most of the year," SAAMA said.
